newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: PARLIAMENT'S ROLE TO CHANGE HIGH COURT LAWS: PM
The Prime Minister says it's Parliament's job to change laws coming out of the High Court if it disagrees with the court's judgement.
John Howard's comments follow concerns raised by the court's Chief Justice in a letter to Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer over the National Party leader's strong criticism of the Wik decision.
Speaking on Sydney Radio 2UE, Mr Howard says the decisions of the High Court are not permanent.
He says the High Court declares the law, and it's the parliament's on-going right to change that law if it believes it's in the interest of the Australian community.
QLD PREMIER ATTACKS HIGH COURT
The Queensland Premier says if the High Court's going to create judge-made law, it has to be accountable and accept criticism.

Rob Borbidge was commenting on concerns raised by the Court's Chief Justice in a letter to the Deputy Prime Minister, that continued criticism of the Court by M-P's could threaten the stability of society.

Mr Borbidge says the Court's decided to assume the role of law-maker, and by doing so is undermining the basic democratic principles of government, and in effect abandoning the doctrine of the separation of powers.
He says the long-held convention preventing politicans from attacking judicial integrity has been broken by the Court, not Mr Fischer.
KENNETT CONDEMNS GRAND PRIX TRACK ATTACK

Victorian Premier, Jeff Kennett, has condemned last night's attack on Melbourne's Grand Prix track as an "act of bastardry". Emergency services workers are this morning cleaning up what remains of a 600-metre diesel slick, deliberately spilled onto the Albert Park track.

Mr Kennett says the spill could have led to a major injury or worse to people who may have driven onto it during the night. The Confederation of Australian Motor Sports will examine the track to make sure it's safe for the preliminary races which start next Thursday.
Police are appealing to any witnesses to come forward.
MINISTERS TO MEET ON NEW DROUGHT POLICY
The Federal Government is planning to take a more pro-active approach to Australia's drought management in a new drought policy.
State and Territory minsters ministers meeting in Melbourne today will be asked to endorse the new policy.
Federal Primary Industries minister, John Anderson, says the current system doesn't help farmers prepare for drought or to become self-reliant.
Mr Anderson says there's a need for an approach that doesn't involve crisis management after a drought's hit.
The Federal Government says it's full implementation may be years away, once the drought breaks and affected farmers recover.
The ministers will also discuss native title and pastoral leases.
TV PROFITS UP
Television broadcasting has improved in profitability.
Figures compiled by the Australian Broadcasting Authority show free-to-air operators reaped a total profits of almost 440-million dollars last financial year.
The ABA says that's an eight percent increase over 1994-95. It was shared among 44 licence holders, with only three of them suffering losses.
The ABA says the commercial television industry has achieved greater profitability by containing costs in a year of below average revenue growth.
POLICE FATALLY SHOOT GUNMAN NEAR DARWIN
Northern Territory police have fatally shot a man in Palmerston near Darwin.
Deputy Police Commissioner Dave Moore says the shooting happened early this morning after police were called to a unit after reports of gun shots.
At the unit in the suburb of Gray, police were confonted by a man armed with a rifle.
Commissioner Moore says the officers retreated, and the gunman opened fire on their car.
He says the police further retreated and called for the gunman to surrender his weapon, but he fired towards the officers, and police returned fire.
One man is dead, and police say a woman at the scene who'd been shot before police arrived, has been taken to hospital.
AUSTRALIA FIRST RALLY IN NSW BORDER TOWN
Leader of the Australia First Party, Independent M-P Graham Campbell, says his new party won't survive with out mainstream support.
The party's holding a rally in the New South Wales border town of Albury tonight with guest speaker Queensland independent Pauline Hanson.
Mr Campbell says he's hoping to recruit new members at the rally.
